title: Choose the home's structure
question: The roll dealt three ways to compose Warlock's home inside the Agentic Factory world. Lock one, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: The timetable floor
options.thesis: Every run is a row, every station a column, and the home reads as the board of where each run has been and is now.
options.viewport: Rail on the left; a top bar with the project and run tallies and the one primary button; the floor as a grid of runs by station with the current cell lit and visited cells carrying their time; the inspector on the right for the run you opened; the warlock composer docked along the bottom.
options.risk: Stations differ per formation, so the column set must follow the selected formation or the grid turns into a sparse matrix.

options.label: The board as the floor
options.lineage: kanban boards and the GitHub Projects board the tasks already sync to
options.thesis: The task lanes are the home: every task card carries its run's station and lamp, so the board and the floor are one screen.
options.viewport: Rail on the left; a top bar with the project, the five lane counts and the one primary button; five lanes (backlog, ready, in progress, in review, done) across the floor, each card showing station, agent, lamp and elapsed; the inspector on the right; the composer as a sheet from the primary button.
options.risk: Lanes are task status, not run position, so a card at in progress hides the handoff rhythm unless the station chip and lamp carry it.

options.label: One line per project
options.lineage: multi-line transit diagrams and the design system's own Line component
options.thesis: Each project is a line on the floor, its runs as station cards on the lane, so the home is the floor at a glance, line by line.
options.viewport: Rail on the left; a top bar with floor-wide tallies and the one primary button; the floor as stacked lines, one per project, each with its formation's stations on a lane and the runs at them as station cards; the inspector on the right; the composer docked along the bottom.
options.risk: Three or more projects push the floor below the fold, so lines need a collapsed height and a sort by activity.
